properties.bedrock_type: Carboniferous Sandstone (Gullane Formation / Craigleith Sandstone bedrock)
properties.mineralogy: Fine-to-medium grained quartz arenite with carbonaceous siltstone interbeds
properties.drainage: Well-draining north-sloping glacial till terrace grading toward the Water of Leith basin

properties.primary_surfacing: Historic whinstone sett drainage gutters alongside modern asphalt carriageway and York/Hailes stone slab pedestrian pavements
properties.wear_characteristics: Surface polished by vehicular traffic, dark bitumen patching, delineated parallel white road markings
properties.micro_grading: Consistent gentle northeast downward slope along the northern boundary of the New Town

properties.groundcover: Queen Street Gardens northern boundary lawn, mature woodland perimeter planting with rich organic leafy canopies directly flanking the right side of the street

properties.primary_building_typology: Georgian Neoclassical Palace-Fronted Terraced Townhouses (designed by Robert Reid and William Sibbald, c. 1802–1808)

structures.name: Heriot Row North Terrace (including 18 Heriot Row - former home of R.L. Stevenson)
structures.roof_geometry: Dual-pitched Scottish Ballachulish slate roof with copper-clad dormer windows, stone chimneys, and ashlar blocking courses
structures.facade_material: Finely dressed Craigleith blonde ashlar sandstone, rusticated ground floors with sunken basement lightwells bridged by stone plinths and cast-iron balustrades
structures.weathering_patina: Historical industrial coal-smoke and soot crusting deep in window architrave reveals, under cornices, and string courses, contrasted against rain-washed honey-toned sandstone faces

period_vehicles: Modern passenger sedans and estate cars parked parallel along both curbs
street_furniture: Black spearhead wrought-iron railings enclosing basement areas
pedestrian_profiles: Occasional pedestrians walking on wide flagstone footpaths

properties.lighting_condition: Low-angle Golden Hour illumination casting long raking warm amber light along the neoclassical sandstone facades with deep, soft elongated shadows
